chapter: Trent's band: Arkansas, Dallas and the Adolphus
title: Co-op rehearsals and head arrangements
summary: Each member leads rehearsals on a different day and sections are written collectively, making many into arrangers and leaders.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: NOW WHAT TIME, AT WHAT POINT DID YOU START HAVING THE GUYS WRITE THEIR OWN ARRANGEMENTS, WERE YOU GUYS STARTING TO MAKE UP YOUR OWN STUFF.

Yeah, after we were at the Adolphis, I guess for about two or three months, we started having having a policy of where we rehearsed at least four days every week and each band had charge of rehearsals. That's the reason so many of the guys in that band turned out to be bandleaders and arrangers becuse maybe on Monday would be my day to start the band, the next day Holder and the next would be somebody else, Trent or somebody else. And a lot of the arrangers that we had, we got them together as a head arranger then different ones would write out different rythms like we had a song

We knew half the time just what number we were going to rehearse each time and we would write out the brass section and maybe some of the reed section and some other guy would do the same thing and then we would get together and that's what we would call a head arranger and between that and a few of the ones that we eventually bought, they developed some marvelous things.
